Don't be the turkey. It was fed for a thousand days, then lost everything.
Every day, a farmer feeds the turkey. And every day, it grows more sure. Humans love me.
Day one hundred. Day five hundred. Day one thousand. Its confidence is at an all-time high.
Then comes the day before the festival. The day the turkey never saw coming.
Investors do the exact same thing with stocks. Let me show you a real one.
Yes Bank. For years it kept rising, and in August twenty eighteen, it touched about four hundred rupees. Its value crossed one lakh crore.
Every month of rising made investors feel safer. Just like the turkey.
So what was the turkey's mistake? Stay till the end, because there were three warning signs you can check in any stock.
September twenty eighteen. The RBI cut the CEO's term short. The stock nearly halved in one month.
March twenty twenty. The RBI took over the board, and capped withdrawals at fifty thousand rupees. The stock crashed about eighty five percent in a day.
Today, six years later, it trades near sixteen rupees. Still about ninety six percent below the peak.
The turkey's mistake? Thinking a long, calm streak means safety. Here are the three warning signs.
One. Loans growing too fast to stressed companies. Two. The promoter pledged his entire stake. Three. The regulator itself raised a red flag.
A long rising chart is not proof of safety. Save this, and follow money in cloud for more Animal Fridays. Or are you still the turkey?
